questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are natural/traditional methods of contraception?
Periodic abstinence, Nirodh, Coitus interruptus, Copper T, Lactational amenorrhea, Cervical cap, Saheli
questions.explanation:
Natural methods: periodic abstinence, coitus interruptus (withdrawal) and lactational amenorrhea. That makes 3.
Nirodh is a male condom and the cervical cap is a female barrier, so both are barrier methods.
Copper T is an IUD.
Saheli is an oral contraceptive pill.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are copper-releasing IUDs?
CuT, Lippes loop, Cu7, LNG-20, Multiload 375, Progestasert
questions.explanation:
CuT: copper-releasing.
Cu7: copper-releasing.
Multiload 375: copper-releasing.
Lippes loop: non-medicated, so it is excluded.
LNG-20 and Progestasert: hormone-releasing, so they are excluded.
The total is 3.
Answer: (2)

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) World population, 1900
(B) World population, 2000

List-II

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) In periodic abstinence, couples avoid coitus from day 10 to day 17 of the menstrual cycle.
(ii) Oral pills inhibit ovulation and implantation and also alter the quality of cervical mucus.
(iii) Diaphragms and cervical caps are disposable barriers meant for single use.
(iv) Tubectomy prevents contraception by stopping the formation of ova.
(v) IUDs inserted within 72 hours of coitus can act as emergency contraceptives.
(vi) Hepatitis-B can be transmitted from an infected mother to the foetus.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: days 10–17 make up the fertile period.
(ii) Correct: this is the stated mode of action of the pills.
(iii) Incorrect: diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are reusable. It is condoms that are disposable.
(iv) Incorrect: sterilisation blocks gamete transport, not gamete formation.
(v) Correct: IUDs or hormones given within 72 hours are effective emergency contraceptives.
(vi) Correct: hepatitis-B and HIV can pass from mother to foetus.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to NCERT, the world population around the year 1900 was approximately:
options: 350 million
2 billion
6 billion
7.2 billion
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that world population was about 2 billion (2000 million) in 1900.
It rose to about 6 billion by 2000 and 7.2 billion in 2011.
350 million is India's population at independence, not the world figure.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Sterilisation prevents conception even though the gonads are not removed.
Reason (R): Surgical intervention in sterilisation blocks the transport of gametes.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Vasectomy and tubectomy act on the ducts (vas deferens and fallopian tube). The testes and ovaries are left in place.
R is true. NCERT states that surgical intervention blocks gamete transport.
R explains A. Because gametes cannot travel through the blocked duct, sperm and ovum cannot meet, so conception is prevented.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Causes of infertility may be physical, congenital, diseases, drugs, immunological or psychological.
(ii) In ZIFT, a zygote or an early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres is transferred into the fallopian tube.
(iii) In ICSI, a sperm is introduced into the uterus of the female.
(iv) Artificial insemination can correct infertility caused by very low sperm counts in the ejaculate.
(v) In artificial insemination, the semen must always be collected from the husband.
(vi) Indian laws permit legal adoption, which is one of the best methods for couples looking for parenthood.
options: Two
Three
Four
Five
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: NCERT lists all of these as possible causes.
(ii) Correct: this is the ZIFT criterion.
(iii) Incorrect: in ICSI, the sperm is injected directly into the ovum in the laboratory.
(iv) Correct: AI treats a male's inability to inseminate or a very low sperm count.
(v) Incorrect: the semen may come from the husband or a healthy donor.
(vi) Correct.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A woman has undergone tubectomy. How does this procedure prevent pregnancy?
options: Ovulation stops completely because the ovaries are removed
The uterus becomes unsuitable for implantation due to hormone release
The ovum and sperm cannot meet because the fallopian tube, where fertilisation normally occurs, is blocked
Menstruation stops permanently, so no ovum is released
questions.explanation:
In tubectomy, a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied. The ovaries are not removed. So option 1 is wrong.
Fertilisation normally takes place in the fallopian tube. The surgical block stops the ovum and sperm from meeting there.
Making the uterus unsuitable for implantation is how hormone-releasing IUDs act, not surgery. So option 2 is wrong.
The procedure blocks the tube; it does not halt ovulation. So option 4 is wrong.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Case 1: A woman cannot produce ova, but her reproductive tract can provide a suitable environment for fertilisation and development. An ovum collected from a donor is placed into her fallopian tube.
Case 2: In another couple, IVF produces an embryo with 16 blastomeres, which is then transferred into the woman's body.
Identify the techniques used in Case 1 and Case 2 respectively.
options: GIFT and IUT
GIFT and ZIFT
ZIFT and IUT
IUI and ZIFT
questions.explanation:
Case 1: A donor ovum is transferred into the fallopian tube of a female who cannot produce ova but can support fertilisation. This is GIFT.
Case 2: An embryo with 16 blastomeres has more than 8 blastomeres, so it must go into the uterus. This is IUT.
ZIFT is used only for a zygote or embryo with up to 8 blastomeres.
IUI transfers semen, not an embryo.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are given in NCERT as probable reasons for the population explosion?
(i) Rapid decline in death rate
(ii) Decline in maternal mortality rate (MMR)
(iii) Decline in infant mortality rate (IMR)
(iv) Increase in number of people in reproducible age
(v) Statutory raising of marriageable age
(vi) Incentives to couples with small families
options: Two
Three
Four
Six
questions.explanation:
(i) to (iv) Correct: NCERT names a rapid decline in death rate, MMR and IMR, together with more people of reproducible age, as probable reasons.
(v) and (vi) Incorrect: these are measures taken to check population growth, not causes of it.
So four of the six are reasons.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding population growth, as described in NCERT, is INCORRECT?
options: World population roughly tripled between 1900 and 2000
According to the 2011 census, India's population growth rate was less than 2 per cent, i.e., 20/1000/year
Statutory raising of the marriageable age of females to 18 years was one of the probable reasons for the population explosion
A rapid decline in death rate, MMR and IMR contributed to the rapid rise in population
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: world population rose from about 2 billion in 1900 to about 6 billion in 2000, roughly three times.
(2) Correct: the 2011 census growth rate was below 2 per cent, i.e., 20/1000/year.
(3) Incorrect: raising the marriageable age (females to 18, males to 21) was a measure to check population growth, not a cause of it.
(4) Correct: falling death rate, MMR and IMR, together with more people of reproducible age, are the probable reasons NCERT gives.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A person who has never had sexual contact with an infected individual can still contract hepatitis-B.
Reason (R): Hepatitis-B is transmitted only through sexual intercourse.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT states that hepatitis-B and HIV can also spread through shared injection needles and surgical instruments, through blood transfusion, and from an infected mother to the foetus.
R is false. Because these non-sexual routes exist, hepatitis-B is not transmitted only through sexual intercourse.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes 'Saheli', the oral contraceptive developed at CDRI, Lucknow?
options: A steroidal pill taken daily for 21 days
A non-steroidal pill taken once a week
A progestogen implant placed under the skin
A copper-releasing device inserted into the uterus
questions.explanation:
Saheli is an oral contraceptive for females developed at the Central Drug Research Institute, Lucknow.
It contains a non-steroidal preparation.
It is a 'once a week' pill with very few side effects and high contraceptive value.
The daily steroidal schedule describes the conventional pills, not Saheli.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: 'Nirodh', a contraceptive widely advertised in India, is a popular brand of which of the following?
options: Female condom
Copper releasing IUD
Male condom
Non-steroidal oral pill
questions.explanation:
NCERT names 'Nirodh' as a popular brand of condom for the male.
A male condom is a thin rubber/latex sheath that covers the penis, so ejaculated semen does not enter the female tract.
The female condom is the tempting wrong choice, but Nirodh is the male product.
The non-steroidal once-a-week oral pill is Saheli, and CuT is a copper IUD.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: 'Saheli', the oral contraceptive developed at the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI), Lucknow, differs from the usual contraceptive pills because it is a:
options: non-steroidal preparation taken once a week
progestogen-estrogen combination taken daily for 21 days
progestogen-only preparation implanted under the skin
hormone-releasing preparation placed inside the uterus
questions.explanation:
NCERT describes Saheli as a new oral contraceptive for females. It contains a non-steroidal preparation.
It is a 'once a week' pill with very few side effects and high contraceptive value.
The usual pills contain steroidal hormones (progestogens or progestogen-estrogen) and are taken daily for 21 days. This makes option (2) the tempting but wrong choice.
Implants and hormone-releasing IUDs are not oral pills at all.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following sexually transmitted infections are NOT completely curable even if detected early and treated properly?
Gonorrhoea, syphilis, genital herpes, hepatitis-B, chlamydiasis, HIV infection, trichomoniasis, genital warts
options: Two
Three
Four
Five
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that, except for hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV infections, the other STIs are completely curable if detected early and treated properly.
The incurable ones in this list are genital herpes, hepatitis-B and HIV, which makes three.
Gonorrhoea, syphilis, chlamydiasis, trichomoniasis and genital warts are all curable.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(a) ZIFT
(b) IUT
(c) GIFT
(d) IUI
List-II
(i) Embryo with more than 8 blastomeres transferred into the uterus
(ii) Semen introduced into the uterus
(iii) Zygote or early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres transferred into the fallopian tube
(iv) Ovum from a donor transferred into the fallopian tube of another female
Choose the correct option.
options: a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii
a-i, b-iii, c-iv, d-ii
a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv
a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii
questions.explanation:
(a) ZIFT matches (iii): a zygote or embryo with up to 8 blastomeres goes into the fallopian tube.
(b) IUT matches (i): an embryo with more than 8 blastomeres goes into the uterus.
(c) GIFT matches (iv): a donor ovum is placed into the fallopian tube of another female.
(d) IUI matches (ii): semen is introduced into the uterus.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Progestasert is an example of a:
options: Copper-releasing IUD
Non-medicated IUD
Hormone-releasing IUD
Barrier method used by females
questions.explanation:
NCERT names Progestasert and LNG-20 as hormone-releasing IUDs.
Copper-releasing IUDs are CuT, Cu7 and Multiload 375.
The non-medicated IUD is Lippes loop.
An IUD is placed inside the uterus. It is not a barrier such as a diaphragm or cervical cap.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Saheli
(b) Combined oral pill
(c) Implant
(d) Emergency contraceptive
List-II
(i) Hormone preparation placed under the skin with a long effective period
(ii) Used within 72 hours of unprotected coitus
(iii) Non-steroidal, taken once a week
(iv) Progestogen–estrogen taken daily for 21 days
questions.explanation:
(a) Saheli is a non-steroidal, once-a-week pill, so it matches (iii).
(b) The combined pill is a progestogen–estrogen preparation taken daily for 21 days, so it matches (iv).
(c) An implant sits under the skin and has a long effective period, so it matches (i).
(d) An emergency contraceptive is used within 72 hours of coitus, so it matches (ii).
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) In vasectomy, a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up.
(ii) Tubectomy can be done through a small incision in the abdomen.
(iii) Surgical sterilisation is highly effective and easily reversible.
(iv) Contraceptives are regular requirements for maintaining reproductive health.
options: One
Two
Three
Four
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: this is how vasectomy is described.
(ii) Correct: tubectomy is done via an abdominal incision or through the vagina.
(iii) Incorrect: sterilisation is highly effective, but its reversibility is very poor.
(iv) Incorrect: contraceptives are not regular requirements for reproductive health. They are used against a natural event, conception.
So two statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements about hormonal and related contraceptive methods is INCORRECT?
options: Hormone-releasing IUDs such as LNG-20, besides acting like other IUDs, make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms
Saheli works on the same principle as the usual pills, being a progestogen-estrogen combination taken once a week
An IUD inserted within 72 hours of unprotected coitus can serve as an emergency contraceptive
Progestogens can be used alone, without estrogen, as pills, injections or implants
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: hormone-releasing IUDs (Progestasert, LNG-20) also make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms.
(2) Incorrect: Saheli is a non-steroidal preparation. It is not a progestogen-estrogen combination, although it is indeed taken once a week.
(3) Correct: NCERT lists IUDs, along with hormones, as emergency contraceptives when used within 72 hours.
(4) Correct: progestogens alone, or in combination with estrogen, are used as pills, injections and implants.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A woman with a regular 28-day menstrual cycle starts menstruating on 25 April. If she and her partner follow the periodic abstinence method as described in NCERT, during which dates should they avoid coitus in that cycle?
options: 25 April to 1 May
4 May to 11 May
5 May to 12 May
12 May to 19 May
questions.explanation:
Day 1 of the cycle is the first day of menstruation, which is 25 April.
April has 30 days, so 30 April is day 6 and 1 May is day 7.
Counting on, day 10 is 4 May and day 17 is 11 May.
Periodic abstinence avoids coitus from day 10 to day 17, the fertile period, so the window is 4 May to 11 May.
Option 3 results from treating 25 April as day 0 instead of day 1.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which year did India start its national-level 'family planning' programmes to attain total reproductive health as a social goal?
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that India's national family planning programmes began in 1951. They were assessed periodically over the following decades.
1971 is a tempting distractor, but that is the year MTP was legalised.
1947 is the year of independence, and 2011 is a census year.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Oral contraceptive pills are taken daily for 21 days, starting preferably within the first five days of the menstrual cycle, and are repeated after a gap of 7 days.
Statement II: These pills inhibit ovulation and implantation and also alter the quality of cervical mucus to prevent or retard the entry of sperms.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Pills are taken daily for 21 days. Menstruation occurs during the 7-day gap, and then the same pattern is repeated.
Statement II is correct. Pills contain progestogens alone or progestogen–estrogen combinations. They act in three ways: they inhibit ovulation, inhibit implantation, and change the cervical mucus.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to NCERT, tubectomy can be performed by removing or tying a small part of the fallopian tube through a small incision made in the:
options: Scrotum only
Abdomen, or through the vagina
Cervix only
Inguinal canal
questions.explanation:
Tubectomy is female sterilisation.
A small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up.
This is done through a small incision in the abdomen or through the vagina.
The scrotal incision belongs to vasectomy, the male procedure. The cervix and inguinal canal are not described as access routes.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: 'Saheli', a new oral contraceptive for females, was developed by scientists at which institute?
options: Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI), Lucknow
All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi
National Institute of Immunology (NII), New Delhi
Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB), Hyderabad
questions.explanation:
NCERT gives Saheli as an example of reproduction-related research in India.
It was developed by scientists at the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI), Lucknow.
The other institutes are well known in Indian biomedical research, but NCERT does not credit any of them with Saheli.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Making the uterus unsuitable for implantation is an effect shared by oral pills and hormone-releasing IUDs such as LNG-20.
Statement II: Saheli is a steroidal preparation that must be taken daily for 21 days, followed by a 7-day gap.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Pills inhibit implantation, and hormone-releasing IUDs (Progestasert, LNG-20) also make the uterus unsuitable for implantation.
Statement II is incorrect. Saheli is non-steroidal and is taken once a week.
The daily 21-day schedule with a 7-day gap applies to the conventional pills, not to Saheli.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The lactational amenorrhea method of contraception has been reported to be effective only up to a maximum of how long after parturition?
options: Two months
Six months
Twelve months
Eighteen months
questions.explanation:
Lactational amenorrhea relies on the absence of ovulation and menstrual cycles during intense lactation after childbirth.
NCERT states that this method is effective only up to a maximum of six months following parturition.
After six months, the chance of conception rises. Longer periods such as 12 or 18 months are therefore unsafe to rely on.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Intra Uterine Devices is incorrect?
options: IUDs increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus
Multiload 375 belongs to the same category of IUDs as CuT
Hormone-releasing IUDs act only by making the uterus unsuitable for implantation and have no effect on sperms
IUDs are one of the most widely accepted methods of contraception in India
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: IUDs in general increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus.
(2) Correct: Multiload 375 and CuT are both copper-releasing IUDs.
(3) Incorrect: Hormone-releasing IUDs also increase sperm phagocytosis and make the cervix hostile to sperms. So they do act on sperms.
(4) Correct: NCERT calls IUDs one of the most widely accepted contraceptive methods in India.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following pairs do BOTH contraceptives act by physically preventing sperms from meeting the ovum, with one of them disposable and the other reusable?
options: Female condom and Multiload 375
Diaphragm and vault
Lippes loop and Nirodh
Nirodh and cervical cap
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Barrier methods include condoms, diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults. Lippes loop and Multiload 375 are IUDs, so options 1 and 3 fail.
Step 2: Diaphragm and vault are both barriers, but both are reusable, so option 2 fails the disposable/reusable condition.
Step 3: Nirodh (male condom) is a disposable barrier, and the cervical cap is a reusable barrier. Only this pair satisfies both conditions.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The early symptoms of most sexually transmitted infections are minor, such as itching, fluid discharge, slight pain and swellings in the genital region.
Statement II: The social stigma attached to STIs encourages infected persons to seek detection and treatment at an early stage.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT describes the early symptoms of most STIs as minor: itching, fluid discharge, slight pain and swellings in the genital region.
Statement II is incorrect. Social stigma, together with mild or absent early symptoms, deters infected people from timely detection and treatment. It does not encourage them.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Early symptoms of most sexually transmitted infections are minor, such as itching, fluid discharge, slight pain and swellings in the genital region.
Statement II: The incidence of STIs is reported to be highest in the 25–40 years age group.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT describes the early symptoms of most STIs as minor: itching, fluid discharge, slight pain and swellings in the genital region.
Statement II is incorrect. All persons are vulnerable, but the incidence is reported to be very high in the 15–24 years age group, not 25–40 years.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which year did the Government of India legalise medical termination of pregnancy (MTP) with strict conditions to prevent its misuse?
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that the Government of India legalised MTP in 1971 with strict conditions to avoid its misuse.
1951 is the year the national 'family planning' programmes began, not MTP legalisation.
2017 is the year of the MTP (Amendment) Act, which modified the existing law rather than first legalising MTP.
1961 has no link to MTP in the chapter.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Condoms used as barrier contraceptives by males and females are made of:
options: a thin rubber/latex sheath
a copper-wound plastic frame
a hormone-releasing silicone rod
a rigid metal cup
questions.explanation:
NCERT describes condoms as barriers made of a thin rubber/latex sheath. They cover the penis in the male, or the vagina and cervix in the female.
A copper-wound plastic frame describes copper IUDs such as CuT.
Hormone-releasing rods are implants placed under the skin.
A rigid metal cup is not a contraceptive device described in NCERT.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Woman X has a Multiload 375 fitted and woman Y has an LNG-20 fitted. Which statement correctly distinguishes the two devices?
options: Only X's device increases phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus
Only Y's device makes the cervix hostile to sperms and the uterus unsuitable for implantation
Only Y's device has to be inserted by a doctor or expert nurse
Only X's device is suitable for spacing children
questions.explanation:
Multiload 375 is a copper-releasing IUD. LNG-20 is a hormone-releasing IUD.
(1) Wrong: every IUD increases phagocytosis of sperms.
(2) Correct: only hormone-releasing IUDs also make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms.
(3) Wrong: all IUDs are inserted through the vagina by doctors or expert nurses.
(4) Wrong: all IUDs are suitable for delaying pregnancy and spacing children.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Hormone-releasing IUDs make the cervix hostile to sperms and the uterus unsuitable for implantation.
Reason (R): Copper ions released from copper-releasing IUDs suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Hormone-releasing IUDs such as Progestasert and LNG-20 make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms. They also increase phagocytosis of sperms, as all IUDs do.
R is true. Cu ions released by CuT, Cu7 and Multiload 375 suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity.
R does not explain A. R describes how copper IUDs work, not hormonal IUDs.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements regarding MTP is INCORRECT?
options: Effective counselling about avoiding unprotected coitus and providing more health care facilities can reverse the trend of illegal abortions
Amniocentesis is completely banned in India because it is misused for female foeticide
Whether to legalise MTP is debated in many countries because of emotional, ethical, religious and social issues
One ground for termination under the Act is that continuing the pregnancy would risk the woman's life or cause grave injury to her physical or mental health
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: NCERT suggests counselling and more health care facilities to reverse this unhealthy trend.
(2) Incorrect: The statutory ban applies only to amniocentesis for sex determination. Amniocentesis is still used to detect genetic disorders such as Down syndrome, haemophilia and sickle-cell anaemia.
(3) Correct: NCERT names these issues as the reason for the debate.
(4) Correct: this is ground (i) of the Act.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The improved programmes now covering wider reproduction-related areas in India are popularly known as:
options: Integrated Child Development Programmes
Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes
National Rural Health Programmes
Universal Immunisation Programmes
questions.explanation:
The family planning programmes started in 1951 were later improved to cover wider reproduction-related areas.
These improved programmes run today under the popular name 'Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes'.
The other options are names of different health or welfare schemes. NCERT does not use them for this purpose.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following sexually transmitted infections are completely curable if detected early and treated properly?
Gonorrhoea, syphilis, genital herpes, chlamydiasis, genital warts, trichomoniasis, hepatitis-B, HIV infection
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that all STIs except hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV infection are completely curable if detected early and treated properly.
The list has 8 infections. Removing the 3 incurable ones leaves 5.
These five are gonorrhoea, syphilis, chlamydiasis, genital warts and trichomoniasis.
Option (1), 3, is the number of incurable infections, which is the tempting mix-up.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Increased health facilities along with better living conditions in the last century had an explosive impact on population growth.
Reason (R): Better health care led to a rapid decline in death rate, maternal mortality rate and infant mortality rate.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: NCERT states that better health facilities and living conditions caused explosive population growth.
R is true: death rate, MMR and IMR fell rapidly.
Fewer deaths while births continue means the population grows faster, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following indicate improved reproductive health of a society?
(i) Decreased maternal and infant mortality rates
(ii) Increased number of medically assisted deliveries
(iii) Increased number of couples with small families
(iv) Better detection and cure of STDs
(v) Increase in MTPs performed by unqualified quacks
(vi) Rising incidence of female foeticide
options: Two
Three
Four
Five
questions.explanation:
(i) Indicator: better post-natal care lowers maternal and infant mortality.
(ii) Indicator: more medically assisted deliveries.
(iii) Indicator: more couples with small families.
(iv) Indicator: better detection and cure of STDs.
(v) Not an indicator: MTPs by quacks are unsafe and can be fatal.
(vi) Not an indicator: female foeticide is a social menace that the law tries to check.
So four statements qualify.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In vasectomy, which structure is cut or tied to prevent conception?
options: Epididymis
Vas deferens
Urethra
Seminiferous tubules
questions.explanation:
Vasectomy is the surgical sterilisation method for males.
A small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small cut on the scrotum.
The epididymis is a tempting choice, but it is not the duct that is cut.
Seminiferous tubules are where sperm are formed, and the urethra is shared with the urinary system. Neither is the target.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are complications that can arise from STIs that are not detected and treated in time?
Pelvic inflammatory disease, ectopic pregnancy, lactational amenorrhoea, still birth, cancer of the reproductive tract, infertility, menopause
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists these complications of untreated STIs: pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), abortions, still births, ectopic pregnancies, infertility and cancer of the reproductive tract.
From the given list, PID, ectopic pregnancy, still birth, reproductive tract cancer and infertility count. That makes 5.
Lactational amenorrhoea is the natural absence of menstruation during intense breast-feeding.
Menopause is a normal physiological event.
Neither of these is an STI complication.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A couple chooses periodic abstinence as their method of contraception. According to NCERT, during which days of the menstrual cycle should they avoid coitus, since ovulation is expected then?
options: Day 1 to day 5
Day 10 to day 17
Day 18 to day 25
Day 21 to day 28
questions.explanation:
In periodic abstinence, the couple avoids coitus during the fertile period, when ovulation is likely.
NCERT gives this period as day 10 to day 17 of the menstrual cycle. Chances of fertilisation are very high in this window.
Days 1–5 are the menstrual phase. Days 18–28 fall in the later luteal phase, after the expected time of ovulation.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In artificial insemination, semen from the husband or a healthy donor may be introduced into the uterus of the female. This particular procedure is called:
options: IUT
ZIFT
IUI
GIFT
questions.explanation:
In artificial insemination (AI), collected semen is placed artificially into either the vagina or the uterus.
When semen is placed into the uterus, the procedure is called IUI (intra-uterine insemination).
IUT is the tempting wrong option. It transfers an embryo with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus, not semen.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a hypothetical society, every individual has physically and functionally normal reproductive organs. However, sex-related crimes and sex-abuse are widespread, and people hold many myths about sex-related aspects. According to the WHO concept, this society is best described as:
options: Reproductively healthy, because all reproductive organs are normal and functional
Reproductively healthy, because reproductive health depends only on physical fitness
Not reproductively healthy, because normal emotional, behavioural and social interactions in sex-related aspects are lacking
Not reproductively healthy, only because contraceptives are not being used regularly
questions.explanation:
WHO defines reproductive health as total well-being: physical, emotional, behavioural and social.
A reproductively healthy society needs normal organs and also normal emotional and behavioural interactions in all sex-related aspects.
Widespread crimes, abuse and myths show that the behavioural and social aspects are lacking, so options 1 and 2 fail.
Option 4 fails because NCERT states that contraceptives are not regular requirements for maintaining reproductive health.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A man with two children opts for vasectomy because the couple wants no more pregnancies. Which statement about his condition after the procedure is most accurate?
options: His testes stop forming sperm, so no gametes are produced
The procedure was done through an abdominal incision and can be easily reversed later
Sperm cannot be transported beyond the blocked vas deferens, so the semen cannot cause conception
He must take daily hormone tablets to keep the method effective
questions.explanation:
Vasectomy blocks gamete transport. It does not stop gamete formation, because the testes are untouched. So option 1 is wrong.
The incision is on the scrotum, not the abdomen, and reversibility is very poor. So option 2 is wrong.
Once the vas deferens is cut or tied, sperm cannot pass into the ejaculate, so conception is prevented.
The method is surgical, so no hormones are needed. Option 4 is wrong.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are valid reasons for MTP as described in NCERT?
(i) Failure of the contraceptive used during coitus
(ii) Pregnancy resulting from rape
(iii) Continuation of pregnancy could be fatal to the mother
(iv) Amniocentesis shows that the foetus is female
(v) Pregnancy following casual unprotected intercourse
options: Two
Three
Four
Five
questions.explanation:
(i) Valid: contraceptive failure can cause an unwanted pregnancy.
(ii) Valid: rape is listed as a cause of unwanted pregnancy.
(iii) Valid: MTP is essential when pregnancy is harmful or fatal to the mother, the foetus or both.
(iv) Not valid: terminating a pregnancy because the foetus is female is female foeticide, which is totally against the law.
(v) Valid: casual unprotected intercourse is listed.
So four reasons are valid.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Over a decade, a district reports a rise in institutional deliveries and a fall in infant mortality. Over the same period, it reports a sharp decline in the number of girls born per 1000 boys, along with a mushrooming of clinics offering prenatal fetal sex testing. Which measure most directly addresses the second trend?
options: Expanding massive child immunisation drives
Strict enforcement of the statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination
Promoting the once-a-week oral pill Saheli
Raising the legal marriageable age of females
questions.explanation:
The first set of trends (more institutional deliveries, lower IMR) shows improving reproductive health.
The falling number of girls, together with clinics doing prenatal sex tests, points to sex determination followed by female foeticide.
NCERT states that the statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination exists to legally check this menace.
Immunisation, Saheli and marriage-age laws address other goals, not sex-selective abortion.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are correct?
(i) They are made of rubber.
(ii) They are inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus.
(iii) They are reusable.
(iv) They must be placed inside the uterus by doctors or expert nurses.
(v) Spermicidal creams, jellies or foams are usually used along with them.
options: Two
Three
Four
Five
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: they are rubber barriers.
(ii) Correct: they cover the cervix and block the entry of sperms.
(iii) Correct: NCERT states they are reusable.
(iv) Incorrect: insertion into the uterus by doctors or expert nurses describes IUDs. These barriers stay in the vagina over the cervix.
(v) Correct: spermicides are used with them to increase efficiency.
So four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Medical termination of pregnancy is considered relatively safe when it is performed
options: during the first trimester, up to 12 weeks of pregnancy
during the second trimester, between 12 and 24 weeks
only after the foetus becomes viable
at any stage, provided two doctors agree
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that MTPs are relatively safe during the first trimester, i.e., up to 12 weeks of pregnancy.
Second-trimester abortions are described as much more risky, so option (2) is wrong.
The two-doctor rule is a legal requirement for 12–24 weeks. It does not make the procedure safer, so option (4) confuses law with safety.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Progestogens, progestogen–estrogen combinations or IUDs are very effective as emergency contraceptives when they are used within how long after coitus?
options: 24 hours
72 hours
7 days
21 days
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that these methods are very effective as emergency contraceptives when used within 72 hours of coitus.
They help avoid a possible pregnancy after rape or casual unprotected intercourse.
The 7-day and 21-day options come from the regular pill schedule, not from emergency use.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Based on NCERT figures, India's population grew more than three-fold between independence and May 2011.
Statement II: Based on NCERT figures, the world population roughly doubled between 1900 and 2000.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I: India grew from about 350 million to over 1.2 billion.
1200/350 ≈ 3.4, which is more than three-fold, so it is correct.
Statement II: The world grew from about 2 billion to about 6 billion.
That is a three-fold rise, not a doubling, so it is incorrect.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following correctly pairs an IUD with the mechanisms of action that NCERT attributes to it?
options: Lippes loop: increased phagocytosis of sperms, and suppression of sperm motility by copper ions
Cu7: increased phagocytosis of sperms, and copper ions suppressing sperm motility and fertilising capacity
Multiload 375: makes the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms
LNG-20: decreases phagocytosis of sperms but makes the cervix hostile to sperms
questions.explanation:
(1) Wrong: Lippes loop is non-medicated and releases no copper.
(2) Correct: Cu7 increases sperm phagocytosis like all IUDs. Its copper ions also suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity.
(3) Wrong: Making the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile are the additional effects of hormone-releasing IUDs, not of copper IUDs like Multiload 375.
(4) Wrong: IUDs increase, not decrease, phagocytosis of sperms.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I:
(a) Hepatitis-B
(b) Trichomoniasis
(c) Use of condoms during coitus
(d) Pelvic inflammatory disease
List-II:
(i) A possible complication of an untreated STI
(ii) A preventive measure against STIs
(iii) Not completely curable; can also spread through blood transfusion
(iv) Completely curable if detected early and treated properly
questions.explanation:
(a) Hepatitis-B is not completely curable. It also spreads through blood transfusion, shared needles and from mother to foetus, so it matches (iii).
(b) Trichomoniasis is completely curable if detected early, so it matches (iv).
(c) Using condoms during coitus is a preventive principle against STIs, so it matches (ii).
(d) PID is a complication of a neglected STI, so it matches (i).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Combined contraceptive pills are taken daily for 21 days, starting preferably within the first five days of the menstrual cycle.
Statement II: During the 7-day gap between two courses of pills, ovulation occurs, so the couple must abstain from coitus during this gap.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT says pills are taken daily for 21 days, preferably starting within the first five days of the cycle.
Statement II is incorrect. The 7-day gap is the time when menstruation occurs, not ovulation. After the gap, the same 21-day pattern is repeated for as long as the woman wants to prevent conception.
Abstaining during a fertile period (days 10 to 17) is part of the periodic abstinence method, not the pill schedule.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about assisted reproductive technologies are correct?
(i) In IVF, ova and sperms are induced to form a zygote under simulated conditions in the laboratory.
(ii) Embryos formed by in vivo fertilisation can also be used for embryo transfer.
(iii) In GIFT, the recipient female cannot produce ova but can provide a suitable environment for fertilisation and development.
(iv) In ICSI, ova and sperms are simply placed together in a dish and allowed to fuse on their own.
(v) In artificial insemination, the semen may come either from the husband or from a healthy donor.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct. In IVF, the zygote is formed in the lab under simulated conditions.
(ii) Correct. NCERT states that embryos from in vivo fertilisation can also be transferred.
(iii) Correct. This is exactly the situation in which GIFT is used.
(iv) Incorrect. In ICSI, a sperm is injected directly into the ovum; the gametes are not left to fuse on their own.
(v) Correct. AI can use semen from the husband or a donor.
So 4 statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): As long as a mother breast-feeds her child fully after parturition, the chances of conception are almost nil.
Reason (R): Ovulation, and therefore the menstrual cycle, does not occur during the period of intense lactation.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. This is the basis of the lactational amenorrhea method. NCERT notes it is effective only up to a maximum of six months after parturition.
R is true. Intense lactation suppresses ovulation, so the cycle does not occur.
R explains A: with no ovulation there is no ovum to fertilise, so conception is very unlikely.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a non-medicated Intra Uterine Device (IUD)?
options: Multiload 375
Lippes loop
LNG-20
Cu7
questions.explanation:
NCERT groups IUDs into three types: non-medicated, copper-releasing and hormone-releasing.
Lippes loop releases neither copper nor hormone, so it is the non-medicated IUD.
Multiload 375 and Cu7 are copper-releasing IUDs.
LNG-20 is a hormone-releasing IUD.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: To be effective as emergency contraceptives after casual unprotected intercourse, progestogens, progestogen-estrogen combinations or IUDs should be used within:
options: 24 hours of coitus
72 hours of coitus
7 days of coitus
21 days of coitus
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that progestogens, progestogen-estrogen combinations or IUDs used within 72 hours of coitus are very effective as emergency contraceptives.
They help avoid a possible pregnancy after rape or casual unprotected intercourse.
The figures 7 and 21 days belong to the regular pill schedule (21 days of pills, then a 7-day gap). They are not the emergency window.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Natural methods of contraception have almost no side effects.
Reason (R): No medicines or devices are used in natural methods of contraception.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: NCERT states that the side effects of natural methods are almost nil.
R is true: these methods involve only timing or behaviour (abstinence, withdrawal, breast-feeding), with no drugs or devices.
R correctly explains A. Side effects come from drugs and devices, so their absence makes side effects negligible.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The copper ions released by a Copper T (CuT) in the uterus help prevent conception mainly by:
options: Inhibiting ovulation from the ovary
Suppressing sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms
Blocking the fallopian tubes permanently
Preventing the formation of sperms in the testes
questions.explanation:
According to NCERT, the Cu ions released by copper IUDs suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms.
Inhibiting ovulation is an action of oral pills, not of copper ions.
Permanent blocking of the fallopian tube describes tubectomy.
A CuT acts inside the female uterus, so it cannot affect sperm formation in the testes.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Condom
(b) Cervical cap
(c) Spermicidal jelly
(d) Cu7
List-II
(i) Increases the contraceptive efficiency of barriers
(ii) Ions released suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity
(iii) Disposable sheath that also protects against STIs
(iv) Reusable rubber barrier covering the cervix
questions.explanation:
(a) Condom – (iii): it is a disposable latex sheath that also protects against STIs and AIDS.
(b) Cervical cap – (iv): it is a reusable rubber barrier covering the cervix.
(c) Spermicidal jelly – (i): it is used along with barriers to increase their contraceptive efficiency.
(d) Cu7 – (ii): it is a copper IUD whose Cu ions suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: NCERT names the statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination as a programme that merits mention among reproductive health strategies. Which other programme is named alongside it?
options: Compulsory sterilisation after the second child
Free distribution of oral pills in schools
Massive child immunisation
Mandatory IVF facilities in every district
questions.explanation:
NCERT says the statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination and massive child immunisation are programmes that merit mention.
Compulsory sterilisation is not an NCERT strategy. Sterilisation is described only as a voluntary terminal method.
NCERT notes that ART facilities such as IVF are available in only a few centres, so they are not mandatory in every district.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Embryos formed by in-vivo fertilisation can also be used for transfer to assist females who cannot conceive.
Statement II: In ZIFT, embryos having more than 8 blastomeres are transferred into the fallopian tube.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT notes that embryos formed by fusion of gametes inside the female (in-vivo fertilisation) can also be transferred to help females who cannot conceive.
Statement II is incorrect. ZIFT transfers a zygote or early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube.
Embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred into the uterus by IUT.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about sexually transmitted infections is INCORRECT?
options: The social stigma attached to STIs discourages infected persons from seeking timely detection and treatment.
All persons are vulnerable to STIs, though incidence is very high in the 15–24 years age group.
Since STIs spread only through sexual contact, a foetus cannot acquire any of them from its infected mother.
Prevention or early detection and cure of STIs are given prime consideration under reproductive health-care programmes.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: social stigma, together with mild or absent early symptoms, delays detection and treatment.
(2) Correct: everyone is vulnerable, and incidence is very high in the 15–24 years age group.
(3) Incorrect: hepatitis-B and HIV can pass from an infected mother to the foetus. They can also spread through blood transfusion and shared needles, so STIs do not spread only through sexual contact.
(4) Correct: prevention and early cure are given prime consideration in reproductive health-care programmes.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Under the MTP (Amendment) Act, 2017, a pregnancy of 16 weeks may be terminated on the opinion of a single registered medical practitioner.
Statement II: For pregnancies lasting more than 12 weeks but fewer than 24 weeks, the Act requires two registered medical practitioners to form the opinion, in good faith, that the required ground exists.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. One registered medical practitioner (RMP) is enough only within the first 12 weeks of pregnancy. A pregnancy of 16 weeks is beyond that limit.
Statement II is correct. Between 12 and 24 weeks, two RMPs must form the opinion in good faith that the required ground exists.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex-determination is one of the programmes taken up to attain reproductive health in India.
Reason (R): In amniocentesis, amniotic fluid is analysed for foetal cells and dissolved substances to test for genetic disorders such as Down syndrome.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT lists the statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex-determination as a programme that merits mention under reproductive health.
R is true. Amniocentesis analyses foetal cells and dissolved substances in amniotic fluid to detect disorders like Down syndrome, haemophilia and sickle-cell anaemia.
However, the ban exists to legally check the increasing menace of female foeticide. Its use in detecting genetic disorders does not explain the ban.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Progestasert, in addition to increasing phagocytosis of sperms, makes the uterus unsuitable for implantation.
Reason (R): Progestasert releases copper ions that suppress sperm motility.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Like all IUDs, Progestasert increases phagocytosis of sperms. Being hormone-releasing, it also makes the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms.
R is false. Progestasert releases a hormone, not copper.
Copper ions are released by CuT, Cu7 and Multiload 375.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A mother who fully breast-feeds her baby has almost no chance of conceiving for up to six months after parturition.
Reason (R): During the period of intense lactation after parturition, ovulation and the menstrual cycle do not occur.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Lactational amenorrhea is a natural contraceptive method that NCERT reports to be effective only up to a maximum of six months after parturition.
R is true. During intense lactation, ovulation and therefore the menstrual cycle do not occur.
R explains A. Without ovulation there is no ovum to be fertilised, so conception is almost nil.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Lippes loop
(B) Cu7
(C) Progestasert
(D) Nirodh
List-II
(I) Hormone-releasing IUD
(II) Barrier method for males
(III) Non-medicated IUD
(IV) Copper-releasing IUD
Choose the correct option.
options: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
questions.explanation:
(A) Lippes loop is a non-medicated IUD, so A matches III.
(B) Cu7 releases copper ions, so B matches IV.
(C) Progestasert releases hormone, so C matches I.
(D) Nirodh is a popular brand of male condom, a barrier method, so D matches II.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (contraceptive method) with List-II (basis of action).
List-I:
(a) Periodic abstinence
(b) Coitus interruptus
(c) Lactational amenorrhea
(d) Diaphragm
List-II:
(i) Ovulation does not occur during intense lactation
(ii) Cervix is physically covered to block sperm entry
(iii) Coitus is avoided during the fertile period
(iv) Semen is not deposited in the vagina
questions.explanation:
(a) Periodic abstinence means avoiding coitus during days 10–17, the fertile period, so it matches (iii).
(b) In withdrawal, the penis is withdrawn before ejaculation, so no insemination occurs. This matches (iv).
(c) Lactational amenorrhea works because there is no ovulation during intense lactation, matching (i).
(d) A diaphragm is a rubber barrier covering the cervix, matching (ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In intra cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI), the embryo is formed in the laboratory.
Reason (R): In gamete intra fallopian transfer (GIFT), the donor ovum is fertilised in the laboratory and the resulting zygote is placed in the fallopian tube.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. In ICSI, a sperm is injected directly into the ovum, so the embryo forms in the laboratory.
R is false. In GIFT, the gamete itself, an unfertilised donor ovum, is transferred into the fallopian tube. Fertilisation then occurs inside the body of the recipient, who provides a suitable environment for fertilisation and development.
R describes ZIFT, not GIFT. ZIFT is the method in which a laboratory-formed zygote is transferred into the fallopian tube.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In India, the female partner is often blamed when a couple is childless, but more often than not the problem lies in the male partner.
Statement II: Since Indian laws do not permit legal adoption, assisted reproductive technologies are the only option for infertile couples seeking parenthood.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT says the female is often blamed, but more often than not the problem lies in the male partner.
Statement II is incorrect. Indian laws do permit legal adoption.
NCERT calls adoption one of the best methods for couples seeking parenthood, given the many orphaned and destitute children in India.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the ZIFT procedure, which of the following is transferred, and to which site?
options: Embryos with more than 8 blastomeres, into the uterus
A zygote or early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres, into the fallopian tube
An unfertilised donor ovum, into the fallopian tube
Semen from a donor, into the uterus
questions.explanation:
ZIFT stands for zygote intra fallopian transfer.
In ZIFT, a zygote or an early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres is placed in the fallopian tube.
Embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are placed in the uterus. That procedure is IUT, not ZIFT.
Transferring a donor ovum into the tube is GIFT.
Introducing semen into the uterus is IUI.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), reproductive health means total well-being in which aspects of reproduction?
options: Physical and functional aspects only
Physical, emotional, behavioural and social aspects
Physical, genetic and hormonal aspects
Emotional and economic aspects only
questions.explanation:
WHO defines reproductive health as total well-being in all aspects of reproduction: physical, emotional, behavioural and social.
Having normal reproductive organs and functions (option 1) is only part of this. WHO's view is broader and includes emotional and social aspects.
Genetic, hormonal and economic aspects are not part of the definition.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: As one measure to check population growth, the legal marriageable ages in India were raised to:
options: 16 years for females and 18 years for males
18 years for both females and males
18 years for females and 21 years for males
21 years for females and 18 years for males
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists the statutory raising of marriageable age as a population control measure.
The age was raised to 18 years for females and 21 years for males.
Option (4) swaps the two ages, and option (2) gives the same age for both, so neither is correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults prevent conception mainly by:
options: increasing phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus
blocking the entry of sperms through the cervix
inhibiting ovulation and implantation
releasing ions that suppress sperm motility
questions.explanation:
These are rubber barriers inserted into the female reproductive tract. They cover the cervix during coitus and physically block sperms from passing through it.
Increased phagocytosis of sperms is an action of IUDs.
Inhibition of ovulation and implantation is how pills work.
Suppression of sperm motility by released ions is the action of Cu ions from copper IUDs.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to NCERT, which group of couples has mostly adopted the 'one child norm'?
options: Elderly rural couples
Young, urban, working couples
Couples in the tribal belts
Couples who are unable to conceive
questions.explanation:
Media campaigns such as 'Hum Do Hamare Do' (we two, our two) promote small families.
NCERT notes that many couples, mostly the young, urban, working ones, have gone further and adopted a 'one child norm'.
Infertile couples cannot choose family size, so option (4) does not fit.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Surgical methods of contraception are generally advised as a 'terminal method' mainly because they:
options: Are effective only for a few months
Have very poor reversibility and are meant to prevent any more pregnancies
Can be self-performed at home
Work only when combined with spermicidal jellies
questions.explanation:
Sterilisation is advised to a partner who wants no more pregnancies.
It is highly effective, but its reversibility is very poor, so it is treated as a permanent, terminal choice.
Option 1 is wrong because sterilisation is long-lasting, not short-term.
Option 3 is wrong because it is a surgical procedure.
Option 4 is wrong because spermicides are used with barriers such as diaphragms.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to NCERT, IUDs are ideal contraceptives for females who:
options: Want to permanently end their ability to conceive
Want to delay pregnancy and/or space children
Mainly want protection against sexually transmitted infections
Want to terminate an established pregnancy
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that IUDs are ideal for females who want to delay pregnancy and/or space children.
Permanent (terminal) prevention of pregnancy is achieved by sterilisation, such as tubectomy.
Protection against STIs is an added benefit of condoms, not of IUDs.
Terminating an established pregnancy is MTP, not contraception.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about embryo transfer is INCORRECT?
options: A zygote formed in the laboratory may be transferred into the fallopian tube by ZIFT
An embryo having exactly 8 blastomeres is transferred into the uterus by IUT
An embryo having 16 blastomeres is suitable for intra uterine transfer
In vitro fertilisation followed by embryo transfer is popularly called the test tube baby programme
questions.explanation:
The rule: zygotes or early embryos with up to 8 blastomeres go into the fallopian tube (ZIFT). Embryos with more than 8 blastomeres go into the uterus (IUT).
An 8-blastomere embryo falls within the 'up to 8' range, so it belongs to ZIFT, not IUT. Option 2 is therefore incorrect.
Option 1 is correct: a lab-formed zygote is transferred by ZIFT.
Option 3 is correct: 16 blastomeres is more than 8, so IUT applies.
Option 4 is correct: IVF-ET is the test tube baby programme.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In ZIFT, early embryos having more than 8 blastomeres are transferred into the fallopian tube.
Statement II: In GIFT, an ovum collected from a donor is transferred into the fallopian tube of a female who cannot produce ova but can provide a suitable environment for fertilisation.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. In ZIFT, the zygote or early embryos with up to 8 blastomeres are transferred into the fallopian tube. Embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred into the uterus (IUT).
Statement II is correct. This is exactly how NCERT describes GIFT (gamete intra fallopian transfer).
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (assisted reproductive technique) with List-II (what it involves).
List-I
(A) ZIFT
(B) IUT
(C) GIFT
(D) ICSI
List-II
(i) Sperm is injected directly into the ovum in the laboratory
(ii) Ovum collected from a donor is transferred into the fallopian tube of another female
(iii) Embryo with more than 8 blastomeres is transferred into the uterus
(iv) Zygote or early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres is transferred into the fallopian tube
options: A-iii, B-iv, C-i, D-ii
A-iv, B-iii, C-ii, D-i
A-iv, B-iii, C-i, D-ii
A-ii, B-iii, C-iv, D-i
questions.explanation:
(A) ZIFT: a zygote or early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres goes into the fallopian tube, so A-iv.
(B) IUT: an embryo with more than 8 blastomeres goes into the uterus, so B-iii.
(C) GIFT: a donor ovum is transferred into the fallopian tube of a female who cannot produce one, so C-ii.
(D) ICSI: a sperm is injected directly into the ovum to form an embryo in the laboratory, so D-i.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following sexually transmitted infections is NOT completely curable even when it is detected early and treated properly?
options: Gonorrhoea
Syphilis
Genital herpes
Trichomoniasis
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists three STIs that are not completely curable: hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV infection.
All the other common STIs are completely curable if detected early and treated properly. These include gonorrhoea, syphilis, chlamydiasis, genital warts and trichomoniasis.
Gonorrhoea and syphilis are serious and well-known infections, so they can seem incurable. They are still curable with early treatment.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Assisted reproductive technologies are presently available only in a very few centres in India, and only a limited number of people can afford them.
Reason (R): These techniques require extremely high precision handling by specialised professionals and expensive instrumentation.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT notes that ART facilities exist in only a few centres in the country, so their benefits reach only a limited number of people.
R is true. These techniques need highly precise handling by specialists and costly instruments.
R explains A, because the need for specialists and expensive equipment is exactly why ART is scarce and costly.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Amniocentesis
(B) MTP (Amendment) Act, 2017
(C) Unqualified quacks
(D) Second-trimester abortion
List-II
(i) Performs the majority of MTPs, illegally and unsafely
(ii) Analysis of fetal cells and dissolved substances in amniotic fluid
(iii) Much riskier than first-trimester termination
(iv) Aims to reduce illegal abortions and the resulting maternal mortality and morbidity
Choose the correct option.
options: A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(iii)
A-(ii), B-(i), C-(iv), D-(iii)
A-(iii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(ii)
A-(iv), B-(ii), C-(iii), D-(i)
questions.explanation:
A–(ii): In amniocentesis, some amniotic fluid is taken to analyse fetal cells and dissolved substances.
B–(iv): The 2017 Amendment Act was enacted to reduce illegal abortions and the maternal mortality and morbidity they cause.
C–(i): NCERT notes that a majority of MTPs are performed illegally by unqualified quacks.
D–(iii): Second-trimester abortions are much riskier than first-trimester ones.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about 'Saheli' is correct?
options: It is a steroidal pill taken daily for 21 days
It is a non-steroidal oral contraceptive taken once a week
It is a hormone-releasing IUD developed in Lucknow
It is an oral contraceptive pill for males
questions.explanation:
Saheli was developed at the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI), Lucknow, as an oral contraceptive for females.
It contains a non-steroidal preparation and is a 'once a week' pill. It has very few side effects and high contraceptive value.
The 21-day daily schedule belongs to the usual progestogen or progestogen-estrogen pills, not Saheli.
Saheli is a pill, not an IUD, and it is meant for females.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are ways in which oral contraceptive pills (progestogen or progestogen-estrogen combinations) prevent pregnancy?
(i) Inhibit ovulation
(ii) Inhibit implantation
(iii) Alter the quality of cervical mucus to retard the entry of sperms
(iv) Release ions that suppress sperm motility
(v) Increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus
(vi) Surgically block the transport of gametes
options: Two
Three
Four
Five
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: pills inhibit ovulation.
(ii) Correct: pills inhibit implantation.
(iii) Correct: pills alter cervical mucus so that sperm entry is prevented or retarded.
(iv) Incorrect: copper ions that suppress sperm motility come from Cu-releasing IUDs.
(v) Incorrect: increased phagocytosis of sperms is an action of IUDs.
(vi) Incorrect: blocking gamete transport is the action of sterilisation.
So three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The female condom covers the vagina and cervix, so ejaculated semen does not enter the female reproductive tract.
Statement II: Like condoms, diaphragms and cervical caps are disposable barriers discarded after single use.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: the female condom covers the vagina and cervix just before coitus, so semen cannot enter the female tract.
Statement II is incorrect: diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are reusable rubber barriers. Only condoms are described as disposable.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about an ideal contraceptive is INCORRECT?
options: It should be user-friendly and easily available.
It should be effective, with no or least side-effects.
It should be irreversible so that pregnancy is prevented permanently.
It should not interfere with sexual drive, desire or the sexual act.
questions.explanation:
NCERT describes an ideal contraceptive as user-friendly, easily available, effective and reversible, with no or least side-effects.
It should also not interfere with sexual drive, desire or the act.
Reversibility is a required feature, so calling irreversibility ideal is wrong.
Sterilisation is described as a terminal method precisely because its reversibility is very poor.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Natural methods of contraception work on the principle of
options: killing sperms inside the female reproductive tract
inhibiting ovulation through hormones
avoiding chances of the ovum and sperms meeting
blocking gamete transport by surgery
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that natural methods work by avoiding the chances of the ovum and sperms meeting. Examples are periodic abstinence, withdrawal and lactational amenorrhea.
Killing sperms describes spermicides, and hormonal inhibition of ovulation describes pills. Surgical blocking describes sterilisation.
No medicine, device or surgery is used in natural methods.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to NCERT, IUDs are considered ideal contraceptives for females who:
options: want a terminal method to prevent any further pregnancy
want to delay pregnancy and/or space children
want protection against STIs along with contraception
want to stop the formation of ova in the ovary
questions.explanation:
IUDs can be removed, so they suit women who wish to delay pregnancy or space children. NCERT calls them one of the most widely accepted contraceptive methods in India.
A terminal method is sterilisation (tubectomy), not an IUD.
Protection against STIs comes from condoms, not IUDs.
IUDs act on sperms and the uterus. They do not stop ova from forming.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are described in NCERT as modes of action of a copper-releasing IUD such as CuT?
(i) Increased phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus
(ii) Suppression of sperm motility
(iii) Suppression of the fertilising capacity of sperms
(iv) Making the cervix hostile to sperms
(v) Inhibition of ovulation
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: all IUDs increase phagocytosis of sperms in the uterus.
(ii) Correct: copper ions suppress sperm motility.
(iii) Correct: copper ions suppress the fertilising capacity of sperms.
(iv) Incorrect: making the cervix hostile to sperms is an extra effect of hormone-releasing IUDs.
(v) Incorrect: inhibiting ovulation is an action of oral pills, injectables and implants.
So three of the statements apply.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: When should a woman preferably begin her course of oral contraceptive pills, and what happens during the 7-day gap after each course?
options: Begin at ovulation; implantation occurs during the gap
Begin within the first five days of the menstrual cycle; menstruation occurs during the gap
