Begin on day 14 of the cycle; ovulation occurs during the gap
Begin on the last day of menstruation; the corpus luteum forms during the gap
questions.explanation:
Pills are taken daily for 21 days, starting preferably within the first five days of the menstrual cycle.
After the 21 days there is a 7-day gap, and menstruation occurs during this gap.
The pattern is then repeated for as long as the woman wants to prevent conception.
Ovulation cannot be the answer, because the pills themselves inhibit ovulation.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following would NOT indicate an improvement in the reproductive health of a society?
options: Decrease in the maternal mortality rate
Increase in the number of medically assisted deliveries
Increase in the infant mortality rate
Better detection and cure of STDs
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists these as signs of improved reproductive health: better awareness, more medically assisted deliveries, better post-natal care, decreased MMR and IMR, more small families, and better detection and cure of STDs.
A rising infant mortality rate points to a decline, not an improvement.
The other three options are all listed indicators.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: 'Saheli', an oral contraceptive for females developed through research encouraged under reproductive health programmes, was developed at:
options: All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi
Indian Agricultural Research Institute, New Delhi
Central Drug Research Institute, Lucknow
National Institute of Virology, Pune
questions.explanation:
Government and non-governmental agencies support research to find new reproductive-health methods or improve existing ones.
One example is 'Saheli', a female oral contraceptive developed by scientists at the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI), Lucknow.
The other institutes listed are not credited with Saheli.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Male and female condoms give privacy to the user.
Reason (R): Both male and female condoms are disposable and can be self-inserted.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: NCERT states that condoms give privacy to the user.
R is true: both male and female condoms are disposable and can be self-inserted.
R explains A: because the user can put the condom on or insert it without a doctor or nurse, privacy is maintained. This differs from IUDs, which must be inserted by doctors or expert nurses.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (measure) with List-II (purpose it serves, as described in NCERT):
List-I
(A) Sex education in schools
(B) Educating fertile couples about birth control options, breast feeding and care of mothers
(C) Creating awareness of social evils like sex-abuse and sex-related crimes
(D) Strong infrastructure, professional expertise and material support
List-II
(I) Medical assistance in pregnancy, delivery, STDs, abortions, infertility
(II) Building up a socially responsible and healthy society
(III) Bringing up socially conscious healthy families of desired size
(IV) Discouraging myths and misconceptions among the young
options: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
questions.explanation:
A-IV: Sex education gives the young correct information, which discourages myths.
B-III: Educating couples about birth control, breast feeding and mother–child care helps bring up healthy families of desired size.
C-II: Awareness of sex-abuse and sex-related crimes helps build a socially responsible society.
D-I: Infrastructure, expertise and material support are needed to give medical care in pregnancy, delivery, STDs and infertility.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Nearly 45 to 50 million MTPs are performed worldwide every year. Roughly what fraction of all pregnancies conceived in a year does this represent?
options: One-half
One-third
One-fifth
One-tenth
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that 45–50 million MTPs are performed in a year all over the world.
This accounts for about 1/5th of the total number of pregnancies conceived in a year.
So roughly one out of every five conceived pregnancies is intentionally terminated.
The other fractions are not supported by the text.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Three infertility cases are described below.
Case P: The husband is unable to inseminate his wife; the wife's reproductive system is normal.
Case Q: The wife cannot produce ova, but her fallopian tube can provide a suitable environment for fertilisation and further development.
Case R: An embryo with about 32 blastomeres has been obtained by in vitro fertilisation and must be transferred.
Which option correctly pairs each case with the technique described in NCERT?
options: P - ICSI, Q - ZIFT, R - IUT
P - Artificial insemination, Q - GIFT, R - IUT
P - Artificial insemination, Q - ZIFT, R - GIFT
P - GIFT, Q - Artificial insemination, R - ZIFT
questions.explanation:
Case P: When the male cannot inseminate, artificial insemination is used. Semen is placed in the vagina or the uterus (IUI).
Case Q: The wife cannot produce ova but has a functional fallopian tube. A donor ovum is transferred into her tube, which is GIFT.
Case R: An embryo with about 32 blastomeres has more than 8 blastomeres, so it goes into the uterus by IUT.
ZIFT is a tempting wrong choice for R. It is limited to embryos with up to 8 blastomeres placed in the fallopian tube.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about natural/traditional contraceptive methods are correct?
(i) Natural methods work on the principle of avoiding chances of the ovum and sperms meeting.
(ii) In coitus interruptus, a thin latex sheath prevents semen from entering the vagina.
(iii) Lactational amenorrhea works because ovulation, and hence the menstrual cycle, does not occur during intense lactation after parturition.
(iv) No medicines or devices are used in natural methods.
(v) Lactational amenorrhea remains a reliable method for more than a year, as long as the mother continues partial breast-feeding.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: this is the basic principle of natural methods.
(ii) Incorrect: in coitus interruptus, the male withdraws the penis just before ejaculation. A latex sheath is a condom, which is a barrier method.
(iii) Correct: there is no ovulation during intense lactation, so menstruation is absent (amenorrhea).
(iv) Correct: this is why side effects are almost nil.
(v) Incorrect: the method needs full breast-feeding and is effective only up to a maximum of six months after parturition.
Correct statements: 3.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In vasectomy, a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum.
Statement II: Surgical methods of contraception prevent conception by stopping the formation of gametes.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. This is how NCERT describes vasectomy, the male sterilisation procedure.
Statement II is incorrect. Sterilisation blocks gamete transport, not gamete formation. Testes and ovaries keep producing gametes, but the gametes cannot pass through the cut or tied vas deferens or fallopian tube.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A contraceptive device is self-inserted by a woman just before coitus. It covers both the vagina and the cervix and is discarded after a single use. Identify the device and an additional benefit it offers.
options: Diaphragm – makes the cervix hostile to sperms by releasing hormones
Female condom – reduces the risk of contracting STIs and AIDS
Cervical cap – reduces the risk of contracting STIs and AIDS
Female condom – makes the uterus unsuitable for implantation
questions.explanation:
Step 1: The device covers the vagina as well as the cervix and is single-use. This fits the female condom. Diaphragms and cervical caps cover only the cervix and are reusable.
Step 2: NCERT credits condoms with protecting against STIs and AIDS.
Step 3: Diaphragms do not release hormones. Making the uterus unsuitable for implantation is an action of hormonal IUDs, not condoms.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to NCERT, which of the following groups contains only sexually transmitted infections that are NOT completely curable, even if detected early and treated properly?
options: Gonorrhoea, syphilis and chlamydiasis
Trichomoniasis, genital warts and hepatitis-B
Syphilis, genital herpes and HIV infection
Hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV infection
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that all the listed STIs except hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV infection are completely curable if detected early and treated properly.
Option (4) contains exactly these three infections.
Option (2) is tempting because it includes hepatitis-B, but trichomoniasis and genital warts are curable.
Option (3) includes syphilis, which is curable.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) In vasectomy, a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum.
(ii) Surgical methods of contraception act by preventing gamete formation.
(iii) Progestogens or IUDs used within 72 hours of coitus are effective emergency contraceptives.
(iv) Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are disposable barriers.
(v) In periodic abstinence, coitus is avoided from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle.
(vi) In embryo transfer techniques, embryos are always transferred into the uterus.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: this is how vasectomy is described.
(ii) Incorrect: sterilisation blocks gamete transport, not gamete formation.
(iii) Correct: these methods, used within 72 hours, work as emergency contraception.
(iv) Incorrect: diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are reusable.
(v) Correct: days 10 to 17 form the fertile period.
(vi) Incorrect: in ZIFT, the zygote or early embryo goes into the fallopian tube.
So 3 statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which assisted reproductive technique is a single sperm injected directly into the ovum to form an embryo in the laboratory?
options: Gamete intra fallopian transfer (GIFT)
Intra cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI)
Intra-uterine insemination (IUI)
Zygote intra fallopian transfer (ZIFT)
questions.explanation:
ICSI is a specialised laboratory procedure. A sperm is injected straight into the cytoplasm of the ovum to form an embryo.
IUI only places semen in the uterus, so fertilisation happens naturally inside the body.
GIFT and ZIFT are transfer procedures. They do not involve injecting a sperm into the ovum.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding medical termination of pregnancy (MTP) in India is INCORRECT?
options: MTP was legalised by the Government of India in 1971 with strict conditions to avoid its misuse
MTPs are considered relatively safe up to 12 weeks of pregnancy, while second trimester abortions are much riskier
A pregnancy that has lasted between 12 and 24 weeks can be terminated on the opinion of just one registered medical practitioner
Worldwide, MTPs account for about one-fifth of the total pregnancies conceived in a year
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct. India legalised MTP in 1971 with strict conditions.
(2) Correct. The first trimester, up to 12 weeks, is relatively safe; second trimester abortions are riskier.
(3) Incorrect. Under the MTP (Amendment) Act, 2017, one registered medical practitioner's opinion is enough only within the first 12 weeks. Between 12 and 24 weeks, two registered medical practitioners must be of that opinion.
(4) Correct. The 45–50 million MTPs performed each year are about 1/5th of conceived pregnancies.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In vitro fertilisation followed by embryo transfer (IVF-ET) is popularly known as:
options: Test tube baby programme
Surrogacy programme
Reproductive and Child Health programme
Gamete bank programme
questions.explanation:
In IVF, ova and sperms are made to form a zygote in the laboratory under conditions that copy those in the body. The embryo is then transferred into the female.
This method is popularly called the test tube baby programme.
The RCH programme is a national reproductive health programme, not an ART method.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Successful implementation of action plans for reproductive health requires strong infrastructural facilities, professional expertise and material support.
Statement II: Medical assistance under reproductive health programmes is required only for pregnancy and delivery, not for menstrual problems or infertility.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT states that infrastructure, professional expertise and material support are essential for implementing these plans.
Statement II is incorrect. NCERT lists many problems needing medical care: pregnancy, delivery, STDs, abortions, contraception, menstrual problems and infertility.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Sexually transmitted infections in females may remain undetected for a long time.
Reason (R): Infected females are often asymptomatic.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: NCERT notes that STIs in females may remain undetected for long.
R is true: infected females often show no symptoms.
With no symptoms, the infected woman has no reason to seek detection, so the infection goes unnoticed. R therefore directly explains A.
The delay can later lead to complications such as PID or infertility.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about oral contraceptive pills is INCORRECT?
options: They contain small doses of progestogens alone or progestogen–estrogen combinations.
They inhibit ovulation and implantation.
They alter the quality of cervical mucus to prevent or retard the entry of sperms.
They release ions that suppress sperm motility within the uterus.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: pills contain small doses of progestogens or progestogen–estrogen combinations.
(2) Correct: they inhibit ovulation and implantation.
(3) Correct: they change cervical mucus so that sperm entry is prevented or slowed.
(4) Incorrect: suppression of sperm motility by released ions is the action of the Cu ions from copper-releasing IUDs, not of pills.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Method X uses no medicines or devices and has almost nil side effects, but its chances of failure are high. Method Y blocks gamete transport and is highly effective, but its reversibility is very poor. Which feature of an ideal contraceptive does each method mainly fail to meet?
options: X – easy availability; Y – user-friendliness
X – effectiveness; Y – reversibility
X – reversibility; Y – effectiveness
X – least side effects; Y – non-interference with sexual drive
questions.explanation:
Method X matches the natural methods, such as periodic abstinence or lactational amenorrhea.
They have almost nil side effects but a high failure rate, so X fails on effectiveness.
Method Y is surgical sterilisation (vasectomy or tubectomy).
It is highly effective, but its reversibility is very poor, so Y fails on reversibility.
Option (3) swaps the two.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Intra cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) is a specialised procedure in which:
options: semen is introduced directly into the uterus of the female
a sperm is directly injected into the ovum to form an embryo in the laboratory
sperms are injected into the fallopian tube along with a donor ovum
an embryo is injected into the uterine wall for implantation
questions.explanation:
ICSI is a laboratory technique for forming an embryo.
In ICSI, a single sperm is injected directly into the cytoplasm of the ovum.
Option 1 describes IUI, a type of artificial insemination, and no embryo is made in the lab.
Options 3 and 4 do not describe any procedure given in NCERT.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In amniocentesis, which material is withdrawn and analysed?
options: A sample of maternal venous blood
Some of the amniotic fluid surrounding the developing foetus
Blood from the umbilical cord after birth
Cervical mucus collected from the mother
questions.explanation:
NCERT describes amniocentesis as removing some of the amniotic fluid of the developing foetus.
The fetal cells and dissolved substances in this fluid are then analysed.
Maternal blood is not sampled in this procedure. Cord blood can only be taken at birth, so it cannot be used for prenatal testing.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Hormone-releasing IUDs such as LNG-20 make the uterus unsuitable for implantation.
Reason (R): Copper ions released by IUDs such as CuT suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT says hormone-releasing IUDs also make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms.
R is true. Copper ions suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity.
However, R describes copper IUDs, while A is caused by the hormone released. So R does not explain A.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): There is a statutory ban in India on the use of amniocentesis for sex determination.
Reason (R): In amniocentesis, amniotic fluid is analysed for fetal cells and dissolved substances, and this can reveal disorders such as Down syndrome, haemophilia and sickle-cell anaemia.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Amniocentesis for sex determination is legally banned in India.
R is true. The procedure tests fetal cells in the amniotic fluid for certain genetic disorders.
However, R does not explain A. The ban exists to check female foeticide, which follows misuse of the test to find the sex of the foetus. Its value in detecting disorders is not the reason for the ban.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A woman is 18 weeks pregnant. Tests show a substantial risk that the child, if born, would be seriously handicapped by physical abnormalities. Under the MTP (Amendment) Act, 2017, which of the following is correct?
options: The pregnancy may be terminated on the opinion of one registered medical practitioner, as for any first-trimester case
Termination is not permitted because the pregnancy has crossed 12 weeks
The pregnancy may be terminated if two registered medical practitioners, in good faith, are of the opinion that the ground exists
Termination is permitted only after amniocentesis confirms the sex of the foetus
questions.explanation:
18 weeks is more than 12 weeks but fewer than 24 weeks. In this window, the Act requires the opinion of two registered medical practitioners, formed in good faith.
A substantial risk of serious physical or mental abnormality in the child is one of the grounds the Act accepts.
A single practitioner's opinion is enough only within the first 12 weeks, so option (1) is wrong.
Using amniocentesis for sex determination is banned, so option (4) is wrong.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which natural contraceptive method does the male partner withdraw his penis from the vagina just before ejaculation, so that insemination is avoided?
options: Periodic abstinence
Coitus interruptus
Lactational amenorrhea
Vasectomy
questions.explanation:
Withdrawal, also called coitus interruptus, is the method in which the penis is withdrawn just before ejaculation. This prevents semen from being deposited in the vagina.
Periodic abstinence avoids coitus during the fertile period, and lactational amenorrhea depends on breast-feeding.
Vasectomy is a surgical method, not a natural one.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following, according to NCERT, indicate improved reproductive health of a society?
(i) Increase in the number of medically assisted deliveries
(ii) Decline in maternal mortality rate and infant mortality rate
(iii) Increase in the number of couples with small families
(iv) Increased use of amniocentesis to find the sex of the foetus
(v) Better detection and cure of sexually transmitted diseases
(vi) Increase in the number of MTPs performed by unqualified persons
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: more medically assisted deliveries are an NCERT indicator.
(ii) Correct: better post-natal care lowers MMR and IMR, which is listed as a sign of improvement.
(iii) Correct: more couples with small families is a listed indicator.
(iv) Incorrect: amniocentesis for sex determination is statutorily banned because it is misused for female foeticide.
(v) Correct: better detection and cure of STDs is a listed indicator.
(vi) Incorrect: MTPs by unqualified quacks are unsafe and can be fatal, so NCERT calls this a disturbing trend.
Four statements (i, ii, iii, v) are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about oral contraceptives are correct?
(i) Pills are taken daily for 21 days, starting preferably within the first five days of the menstrual cycle.
(ii) After the 21-day course, a gap of 7 days is given, during which menstruation occurs.
(iii) Pills inhibit ovulation and implantation and alter the quality of cervical mucus.
(iv) Saheli contains a steroidal preparation.
(v) Saheli was developed at the Central Drug Research Institute, Lucknow.
(vi) Saheli has to be taken once every day.
options: Three
Four
Five
Two
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: this is the stated 21-day regimen.
(ii) Correct: a 7-day gap follows, during which menstruation occurs.
(iii) Correct: pills inhibit ovulation and implantation and alter cervical mucus to retard the entry of sperms.
(iv) Incorrect: Saheli is a non-steroidal preparation.
(v) Correct: it was developed at CDRI, Lucknow.
(vi) Incorrect: Saheli is a once-a-week pill.
So four statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Read the statements:
Statement I: Reproductive health refers only to the presence of healthy reproductive organs with normal functions.
Statement II: Introducing sex education in schools helps discourage children from believing in myths and misconceptions about sex-related aspects.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. Healthy organs with normal functions is only the simple meaning of the term. Reproductive health has a broader perspective that also includes emotional, behavioural and social aspects.
Statement II is correct. NCERT says sex education in schools gives the young the right information, which discourages myths and misconceptions.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) ZIFT
(B) IUT
(C) GIFT
(D) IUI
List-II
(i) Transfer of an ovum from a donor into the fallopian tube of another female
(ii) Semen introduced into the uterus of the female
(iii) Transfer of zygote or early embryo (up to 8 blastomeres) into the fallopian tube
(iv) Transfer of embryo with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus
Choose the correct answer.
options: A-(iii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(ii)
A-(iv), B-(iii), C-(i), D-(ii)
A-(iii), B-(iv), C-(ii), D-(i)
A-(i), B-(iv), C-(iii), D-(ii)
questions.explanation:
A-(iii): ZIFT places a zygote or early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres in the fallopian tube.
B-(iv): IUT places an embryo with more than 8 blastomeres in the uterus.
C-(i): GIFT transfers a donor ovum into the fallopian tube of a female who cannot produce ova.
D-(ii): IUI introduces semen into the uterus.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Lippes loop
(B) Multiload 375
(C) Progestasert
(D) Saheli
List-II
(i) Once-a-week non-steroidal oral pill
(ii) Hormone-releasing IUD
(iii) Non-medicated IUD
(iv) Copper-releasing IUD
options: A-iii, B-iv, C-ii, D-i
A-iv, B-iii, C-ii, D-i
A-iii, B-ii, C-iv, D-i
A-ii, B-iv, C-iii, D-i
questions.explanation:
(A) Lippes loop is a non-medicated IUD, so A-iii.
(B) Multiload 375 is a copper-releasing IUD, like CuT and Cu7, so B-iv.
(C) Progestasert is a hormone-releasing IUD, like LNG-20, so C-ii.
(D) Saheli is a once-a-week non-steroidal oral pill developed at CDRI, Lucknow, so D-i.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In ZIFT, a zygote or an early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres is transferred into the fallopian tube.
Statement II: In GIFT, an embryo formed by in vitro fertilisation is transferred into the fallopian tube of a female who cannot conceive.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. ZIFT transfers a zygote or an early embryo with up to 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube. Embryos with more than 8 blastomeres go into the uterus by IUT.
Statement II is incorrect. GIFT transfers a gamete, that is, a donor ovum, into the fallopian tube, not an embryo.
The recipient in GIFT is a female who cannot produce ova but can provide a suitable environment for fertilisation and development.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Intentional or voluntary termination of pregnancy before full term is also known as
options: spontaneous abortion
induced abortion
ectopic pregnancy
still birth
questions.explanation:
NCERT defines MTP as intentional or voluntary termination of pregnancy before full term. It is also called induced abortion.
A spontaneous abortion happens naturally, without deliberate intervention, so it is not MTP.
Ectopic pregnancy and still birth are listed in the chapter as complications of STIs, not as names for MTP.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Hepatitis-B can be acquired by a person even without sexual contact with an infected individual.
Reason (R): Hepatitis-B is completely curable if detected early and treated properly.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Hepatitis-B, like HIV, can also spread through shared injection needles and surgical instruments, blood transfusion, or from an infected mother to the foetus.
R is false. NCERT lists hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV as the exceptions that are not completely curable.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Vasectomy
(b) Tubectomy
(c) Copper T
(d) Oral pills
List-II
(i) Part of fallopian tube removed or tied
(ii) Inhibit ovulation and implantation
(iii) Small incision on the scrotum
(iv) Cu ions suppress sperm motility
options: a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii
a-i, b-iii, c-iv, d-ii
a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv
a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii
questions.explanation:
(a) Vasectomy: the vas deferens is cut or tied through a small scrotal incision, so a-iii.
(b) Tubectomy: a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied, so b-i.
(c) Copper T: the copper ions it releases suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity, so c-iv.
(d) Oral pills: they inhibit ovulation and implantation and alter cervical mucus, so d-ii.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: IUDs are inserted into the uterus through the vagina by doctors or expert nurses.
Statement II: An IUD inserted within 72 hours of coitus can act as an effective emergency contraceptive.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT says IUDs are inserted into the uterus through the vagina by doctors or expert nurses. Unlike condoms, they are not self-inserted.
Statement II is correct. NCERT lists IUDs, along with progestogen or progestogen-estrogen preparations, as very effective emergency contraceptives when used within 72 hours of coitus.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A woman had unprotected intercourse about 48 hours ago and wants to avoid a possible pregnancy. Based on NCERT, which of the following is the appropriate option?
options: Start a regular 21-day course of pills from the first day of her next menstrual cycle
Insert a diaphragm with spermicidal cream now
Take a progestogen or progestogen–estrogen preparation, or have an IUD inserted, since she is within 72 hours
Rely on the lactational amenorrhea method for the next six months
questions.explanation:
Hormonal preparations or IUDs used within 72 hours of coitus are very effective emergency contraceptives, and 48 hours falls within this window.
Starting regular pills later does nothing about this act of coitus.
A diaphragm only works as a barrier during coitus, so inserting it now is useless.
Lactational amenorrhea applies only to a mother fully breast-feeding after parturition.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Each of the following sexually transmitted infections is detected early and treated properly. Which one would still NOT be completely curable, according to NCERT?
options: Gonorrhoea
Genital herpes
Trichomoniasis
Syphilis
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that, except for hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV infections, the other STIs are completely curable if detected early and treated properly.
Gonorrhoea, trichomoniasis and syphilis are therefore curable with early, proper treatment.
Genital herpes is one of the three listed exceptions, so it is not completely curable.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are mentioned in NCERT as possible later complications of sexually transmitted infections that are not detected and treated in time?
Pelvic inflammatory disease, ectopic pregnancy, sickle-cell anaemia, still birth, cancer of the reproductive tract, infertility, Down syndrome
questions.explanation:
Listed complications of untreated STIs: pelvic inflammatory disease, ectopic pregnancy, still birth, cancer of the reproductive tract and infertility. That makes 5 items. NCERT also lists abortions, which is not among the options given.
Sickle-cell anaemia and Down syndrome are genetic disorders. NCERT mentions them only in the context of amniocentesis, not as STI complications.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to NCERT, which of the following sexually transmitted infections is considered the most dangerous?
options: Gonorrhoea
HIV infection leading to AIDS
Trichomoniasis
Genital warts
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists gonorrhoea, syphilis, genital herpes, chlamydiasis, genital warts, trichomoniasis, hepatitis-B and HIV as common STIs.
Of these, HIV infection, which leads to AIDS, is described as the most dangerous.
Gonorrhoea, trichomoniasis and genital warts are completely curable if detected early and treated properly.
HIV infection cannot be completely cured.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Natural methods of contraception, such as periodic abstinence and withdrawal, have almost nil side effects.
Reason (R): Natural methods of contraception have a high chance of failure.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Natural methods use no medicines or devices, so side effects are almost nil.
R is true. NCERT states that the chances of failure of these methods are high.
R does not explain A. The near absence of side effects comes from not using drugs or devices, not from the high failure rate. The two facts are independent.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (contraceptive) with List-II (its main mode of action):
List-I
(A) Lippes loop
(B) Multiload 375
(C) LNG-20
(D) Vasectomy
List-II
(I) Blocks transport of gametes
(II) Increases phagocytosis of sperms, with no drug or metal ions released
(III) Releases ions that suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity
(IV) Makes the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms
options: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I
A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I
A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
questions.explanation:
(A) Lippes loop is a non-medicated IUD. It acts only by increasing phagocytosis of sperms, so A-II.
(B) Multiload 375 is a copper-releasing IUD. Its Cu ions suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity, so B-III.
(C) LNG-20 is a hormone-releasing IUD. It makes the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms, so C-IV.
(D) Vasectomy is a surgical method that blocks gamete transport, so D-I.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about amniocentesis is INCORRECT?
options: A sample of the amniotic fluid surrounding the developing foetus is withdrawn
Both the fetal cells and the substances dissolved in the fluid are analysed
It can detect a chromosomal disorder like Down syndrome as well as single-gene disorders like haemophilia
Its use is completely banned in India, including for detecting genetic disorders
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: amniotic fluid of the developing foetus is sampled.
(2) Correct: NCERT says both fetal cells and dissolved substances are analysed.
(3) Correct: NCERT lists Down syndrome (chromosomal) and haemophilia and sickle-cell anaemia (gene disorders).
(4) Incorrect: the statutory ban applies only to sex determination. Genetic testing remains permitted.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are modes of action of oral contraceptive pills?
(i) Inhibition of ovulation
(ii) Increased phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus
(iii) Inhibition of implantation
(iv) Blocking of gamete transport by cutting the fallopian tube
(v) Altering the quality of cervical mucus
(vi) Suppression of sperm motility by copper ions
options: Two
Three
Four
Five
questions.explanation:
(i) Yes: pills inhibit ovulation.
(ii) No: increased phagocytosis of sperms is an action of IUDs.
(iii) Yes: pills inhibit implantation.
(iv) No: blocking gamete transport describes tubectomy.
(v) Yes: pills alter the cervical mucus.
(vi) No: suppression of sperm motility is due to Cu ions from copper IUDs.
This gives three modes of action.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Diaphragms and cervical caps prevent conception by blocking the entry of sperms through the cervix.
Reason (R): Spermicidal creams, jellies and foams are usually used along with these barriers.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are rubber barriers that cover the cervix during coitus and block sperm entry.
R is true. Spermicides are used along with these barriers to increase their contraceptive efficiency.
However, R does not explain how the barrier itself works. The barrier acts by physical blocking, whereas spermicides only add extra efficiency.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following barrier contraceptives, in addition to preventing conception, also gives the user protection against sexually transmitted infections and AIDS?
options: Cervical cap
Diaphragm
Condom
Vault
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: condoms are thin rubber/latex sheaths that cover the penis, or the vagina and cervix, so semen does not enter the female tract.
Their use has increased because they also protect the user from STIs and AIDS.
Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults only cover the cervix to block sperm entry. They are not credited with STI protection.
The tempting choice, the diaphragm, is reusable and blocks sperms but is not described as protecting against STIs/AIDS.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about barrier methods of contraception:
(i) Male and female condoms are disposable and can be self-inserted, giving privacy to the user.
(ii) Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are made of rubber and are reusable.
(iii) Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults prevent conception by covering the cervix and blocking the entry of sperms through it.
(iv) Spermicidal creams, jellies and foams are used to replace diaphragms and cervical caps because the rubber barriers are ineffective by themselves.
How many of the above statements are correct?
options: One
Two
Three
Four
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: both male and female condoms are disposable, self-inserted and give privacy.
(ii) Correct: diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are rubber barriers that are reusable.
(iii) Correct: they cover the cervix during coitus and block sperm entry through the cervix.
(iv) Incorrect: spermicidal creams, jellies and foams are used along with these barriers to increase their contraceptive efficiency, not to replace them.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about natural methods of contraception is INCORRECT?
options: The period from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle is called the fertile period because chances of fertilisation are very high then.
Lactational amenorrhea is reliable for as long as the mother continues breast-feeding, with no time limit.
Natural methods have a high chance of failure.
During intense lactation after parturition, both ovulation and the menstrual cycle are absent.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: ovulation is expected during days 10–17, so the chances of fertilisation are high.
(2) Incorrect: lactational amenorrhea is effective only with full breast-feeding and only up to a maximum of six months after parturition.
(3) Correct: NCERT notes that the failure rate of natural methods is high.
(4) Correct: this is the very basis of the lactational amenorrhea method.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): India legalised MTP only with strict conditions, and these restrictions are especially important in the Indian context.
Reason (R): Indiscriminate and illegal female foeticides are reported to be high in India.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. MTP was legalised in 1971 with strict conditions to avoid its misuse.
R is true. NCERT reports that illegal female foeticides are high in India.
NCERT states that the restrictions are all the more important precisely to check such indiscriminate female foeticides. So R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Infections or diseases transmitted through sexual intercourse are collectively known as STIs. By which other two names are they also known?
options: Venereal diseases (VD) and reproductive tract infections (RTI)
Pelvic inflammatory diseases (PID) and venereal diseases (VD)
Reproductive tract infections (RTI) and congenital disorders
Autoimmune diseases and venereal diseases (VD)
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that diseases transmitted through sexual intercourse are collectively called sexually transmitted infections (STI). They are also called venereal diseases (VD) or reproductive tract infections (RTI).
PID is a complication of untreated STIs. It is not another name for them, which rules out option (2).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are cited in NCERT as indicators of improved reproductive health in society?
(i) Increased number of medically assisted deliveries
(ii) Decreased maternal mortality rate
(iii) Increased number of couples with small families
(iv) Rising incidence of STIs in the 15–24 age group
(v) Better post-natal care
(vi) Increase in average family size
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: this is a listed indicator.
(ii) Correct: falling MMR shows improvement.
(iii) Correct: more small families is listed.
(iv) Incorrect: rising STIs would mean worse reproductive health.
(v) Correct: better post-natal care is listed.
(vi) Incorrect: NCERT links improvement with smaller families, not larger ones.
So 4 statements qualify.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A diagram shows a small incision made on the scrotum, and a small part of a duct is cut out and its ends tied. Which statement correctly describes this procedure?
options: It is tubectomy, and it stops ovum formation
It is vasectomy, and it stops sperm formation in the testes
It is vasectomy, and it blocks the transport of sperms
It is tubectomy, and it blocks the transport of ova
questions.explanation:
An incision on the scrotum with removal or tying of part of the vas deferens is vasectomy, the male sterilisation method.
Surgical methods block gamete transport. They do not stop gamete formation, because spermatogenesis in the testes continues.
Tubectomy acts on the fallopian tube through the abdomen or vagina, so options (1) and (4) do not match the diagram.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the periodic abstinence method of contraception, a couple avoids coitus during which days of the menstrual cycle?
options: Day 1 to day 5
Day 10 to day 17
Day 18 to day 25
Day 21 to day 28
questions.explanation:
Periodic abstinence means avoiding coitus during the days when ovulation is expected.
NCERT places this window from day 10 to day 17 of the menstrual cycle.
Days 1–5 are the menstrual phase, and days 21–28 fall late in the secretory phase, after ovulation. So these are not the targeted days.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I:
(a) Hepatitis-B
(b) Trichomoniasis
(c) Pelvic inflammatory disease
(d) Avoiding sex with unknown or multiple partners
List-II:
(i) A complication that may follow an untreated STI
(ii) An STI that can also spread through shared needles and blood transfusion and is not completely curable
(iii) An STI that is completely curable if detected early and treated properly
(iv) A simple principle for preventing STIs
questions.explanation:
(a) Hepatitis-B: it also spreads through needles, blood and from mother to foetus, and it is not completely curable, so (ii).
(b) Trichomoniasis: it is not among the exceptions, so it is curable if detected early, giving (iii).
(c) PID: NCERT names it as a later complication of untreated STIs, so (i).
(d) Avoiding unknown or multiple partners is a preventive principle, so (iv).
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A woman had casual unprotected intercourse a day ago and wants to avoid a possible pregnancy. Which of the following is an effective emergency contraceptive option according to NCERT?
options: Using a diaphragm with spermicidal jelly now
Inserting an IUD within 72 hours of coitus
Following periodic abstinence from day 10 to 17 of the cycle
Undergoing tubectomy
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that emergency contraception is possible within 72 hours of coitus. Two options are given: progestogens or progestogen-estrogen combinations, or an IUD.
A diaphragm works only if it is in place during coitus, so using it afterwards cannot stop fertilisation that may already be under way.
Periodic abstinence is a preventive method for the future, not an emergency measure.
Tubectomy is a terminal, poorly reversible surgical method. It is not an emergency option.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Saheli, an oral contraceptive for females, was developed by scientists at the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI), Lucknow.
Statement II: Saheli is a steroidal preparation that must be taken once every day.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT states that Saheli was developed at CDRI, Lucknow.
Statement II is incorrect. Saheli contains a non-steroidal preparation and is a 'once a week' pill. It has very few side effects and high contraceptive value.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A woman using a progestogen implant does not need to take a contraceptive dose every day, unlike a woman using oral pills.
Reason (R): Implants act in a way similar to pills, but their effective period is much longer.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: an implant is placed under the skin and keeps working, so no daily dose is needed.
R is true: NCERT states that injections and implants act like pills, but their effective periods are much longer.
R explains A: the longer effective period is exactly why daily intake is unnecessary.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Besides sexual contact, which of the following STIs can also be transmitted by sharing injection needles, by blood transfusion, or from an infected mother to the foetus?
options: Trichomoniasis
Gonorrhoea
Hepatitis-B
Genital warts
questions.explanation:
NCERT names hepatitis-B and HIV as STIs that can also spread in other ways.
These routes are sharing injection needles or surgical instruments, blood transfusion, and from an infected mother to the foetus.
Trichomoniasis, gonorrhoea and genital warts are not described as spreading through needles or transfusion.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A woman is 18 weeks pregnant. Continuing the pregnancy carries a substantial risk that the child would be born seriously handicapped. Under the MTP (Amendment) Act, 2017, which statement correctly describes her situation?
options: MTP is not permitted, because termination is allowed only within the first 12 weeks
MTP can be done on the opinion of one registered medical practitioner, as the pregnancy is under 24 weeks
MTP can be done if two registered medical practitioners form the opinion, in good faith, that the required ground exists
MTP can be done only if the pregnancy threatens the life of the mother, not for foetal abnormality
questions.explanation:
The Act allows termination within the first 12 weeks on the opinion of one registered medical practitioner (RMP).
Between 12 and 24 weeks, two RMPs must form the opinion, in good faith, that the ground exists.
At 18 weeks, she falls in this second window, so option (3) is correct.
Option (4) fails because the risk of serious physical or mental abnormality in the child is itself a valid ground.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A couple is infertile because the husband has a very low sperm count in his ejaculate, while the wife's reproductive system is normal. Which simple technique does NCERT suggest for such cases?
options: Artificial insemination (AI)
Gamete intra fallopian transfer (GIFT)
Tubectomy
Lactational amenorrhea
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that artificial insemination can correct infertility caused by two problems: the male partner being unable to inseminate the female, or a very low sperm count.
In AI, semen from the husband or a healthy donor is introduced into the vagina or the uterus.
GIFT is meant for a female who cannot produce ova.
Tubectomy and lactational amenorrhea are contraceptive methods, not treatments for infertility.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A woman delivered a baby eight months ago and has been breast-feeding since then. She has not used any other contraceptive, believing breast-feeding alone protects her. Based on NCERT, what is the most appropriate assessment of her situation?
options: She is fully protected, because ovulation never resumes while a mother is breast-feeding.
She is at risk of conception, because the method is reported to be effective only up to six months after parturition.
She is at risk only because lactational amenorrhea works through hormones that cause side effects.
She is protected, because lactational amenorrhea also prevents implantation for up to two years.
questions.explanation:
Lactational amenorrhea works because ovulation and the cycle do not occur during intense lactation after parturition.
NCERT reports that this method is effective only up to a maximum of six months after delivery.
At eight months she is beyond this limit, so ovulation may have resumed.
Option 1 ignores this limit. Options 3 and 4 invent a hormonal or implantation-blocking action that this method does not have.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Saheli
(B) Amniocentesis
(C) Family planning programmes in India
(D) Statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination
List-II
(i) Initiated in 1951
(ii) Non-steroidal, once-a-week oral contraceptive
(iii) Legal check on female foeticide
(iv) Analysis of fetal cells in amniotic fluid
options: A-ii, B-iv, C-i, D-iii
A-ii, B-iii, C-i, D-iv
A-iv, B-ii, C-iii, D-i
A-i, B-iv, C-ii, D-iii
questions.explanation:
(A) Saheli is a non-steroidal, once-a-week pill developed at CDRI, so A matches (ii).
(B) Amniocentesis involves analysing fetal cells in amniotic fluid, so B matches (iv).
(C) India's family planning programmes began in 1951, so C matches (i).
(D) The ban exists to legally check female foeticide, so D matches (iii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed in NCERT among the possible ill-effects of contraceptive use?
options: Abdominal pain
Irregular menstrual bleeding
Breast cancer
Osteoporosis
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists these possible ill-effects of contraceptives: nausea, abdominal pain, breakthrough bleeding, irregular menstrual bleeding and even breast cancer.
It adds that they are not very significant but should not be totally ignored.
Abdominal pain, irregular bleeding and breast cancer all appear in this list.
Osteoporosis is not mentioned.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(a) Lippes loop
(b) Multiload 375
(c) LNG-20
(d) Nirodh
List-II
(i) Hormone-releasing IUD
(ii) Barrier method for males
(iii) Non-medicated IUD
(iv) Copper-releasing IUD
questions.explanation:
(a) Lippes loop is a non-medicated IUD, so it matches (iii).
(b) Multiload 375 is a copper-releasing IUD, like CuT and Cu7, so it matches (iv).
(c) LNG-20 is a hormone-releasing IUD, like Progestasert, so it matches (i).
(d) Nirodh is a popular brand of male condom, a barrier method, so it matches (ii).
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about surgical methods of contraception and the side effects of contraceptives are correct?
(i) In vasectomy, a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum.
(ii) In tubectomy, a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up through a small incision in the abdomen or through the vagina.
(iii) Sterilisation prevents conception by stopping the formation of sperms or ova in the gonads.
(iv) Surgical methods are highly effective and are easily reversed whenever the couple wants another child.
(v) Breakthrough bleeding and even breast cancer are among the possible ill-effects of contraceptives.
options: Two
Three
Four
Five
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: in vasectomy the vas deferens is cut or tied through a small scrotal incision.
(ii) Correct: in tubectomy the fallopian tube is cut or tied through a small abdominal incision or through the vagina.
(iii) Incorrect: the gonads keep producing gametes. The surgery only blocks gamete transport.
(iv) Incorrect: these methods are highly effective, but their reversibility is very poor. That is why they are called terminal methods.
(v) Correct: NCERT lists nausea, abdominal pain, breakthrough bleeding, irregular menstrual bleeding and even breast cancer as possible ill-effects.
Correct statements = 3.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following pairs are correctly matched?
(i) Amniocentesis – analysis of fetal cells and dissolved substances in amniotic fluid
(ii) Fertile period – day 10 to day 17 of the menstrual cycle
(iii) Nirodh – popular brand of female condom
(iv) Infertility – inability to conceive even after 2 years of unprotected sexual cohabitation
(v) Age group with very high incidence of STIs – 25 to 35 years
(vi) Statutory marriageable age of females – 21 years
options: Two
Four
Five
Three
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: amniocentesis analyses fetal cells and dissolved substances in amniotic fluid.
(ii) Correct: days 10–17, when ovulation is expected, form the fertile period.
(iii) Incorrect: Nirodh is a male condom.
(iv) Correct: this matches NCERT's summary definition of infertility.
(v) Incorrect: STI incidence is very high in the 15–24 age group.
(vi) Incorrect: the marriageable age was raised to 18 for females and 21 for males.
So three pairs are correct.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The selection and use of a suitable contraceptive method should always be done in consultation with qualified medical professionals.
Statement II: Since ill-effects of contraceptives such as nausea and breakthrough bleeding are not very significant, they can be totally ignored.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT emphasises that the choice and use of a contraceptive should be made with qualified medical professionals.
Statement II is incorrect. NCERT says the possible ill-effects (nausea, abdominal pain, breakthrough or irregular bleeding, even breast cancer) are not very significant. However, they should not be totally ignored.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to NCERT, which of the following is a probable reason for the rapid growth of India's population in the last century?
options: A steep rise in the infant mortality rate (IMR)
A rapid decline in the death rate and in the maternal mortality rate (MMR)
A decrease in the number of people in the reproducible age group
Raising the legal marriageable age of females to 18 years
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists the probable reasons for population explosion: a rapid decline in death rate, MMR and IMR, and an increase in the number of people in the reproducible age.
Option (1) fails: IMR fell. It did not rise.
Option (3) is the opposite of the fact, because the reproducible age group increased.
Option (4) is a measure taken to check population growth, not a cause of it.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A woman is 18 weeks pregnant. Amniocentesis shows a substantial risk that the child, if born, would suffer from such serious physical abnormalities as to be seriously handicapped. According to the MTP (Amendment) Act, 2017 as described in NCERT, which option is correct?
options: The pregnancy cannot be legally terminated because it has crossed 12 weeks
The pregnancy can be terminated on the opinion of one registered medical practitioner, since a genetic disorder is involved
The pregnancy can be terminated if two registered medical practitioners form the opinion, in good faith, that this ground exists
The pregnancy cannot be terminated because amniocentesis is statutorily banned in India
questions.explanation:
At 18 weeks, the pregnancy falls in the 12–24 week window, so the opinion of two RMPs in good faith is required. This rules out option (2).
A substantial risk of serious physical or mental abnormality in the child is one of the two legal grounds, so termination is permitted.
Option (1) is wrong because the law allows termination up to 24 weeks on these grounds.
Option (4) is wrong because amniocentesis is banned only for sex determination, not for detecting genetic disorders.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements regarding strategies to attain reproductive health in India is INCORRECT?
options: Creating awareness about reproduction-related aspects and providing facilities and support are the major tasks of RCH programmes.
Spreading reproductive health information is solely the responsibility of governmental agencies through audio-visual and print media; parents and teachers have no defined role.
Educating people about equal opportunities for the male and the female child is part of creating awareness for healthy families.
Massive child immunisation is mentioned as one of the programmes meriting mention in reproductive health care.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: awareness and providing facilities and support are the major RCH tasks.
(2) Incorrect: both governmental and non-governmental agencies use media to spread information. Parents, close relatives, teachers and friends also play a major role.
(3) Correct: equal opportunities for male and female children is listed among the topics to educate people about.
(4) Correct: massive child immunisation is named alongside the ban on amniocentesis for sex-determination.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the simple principles suggested in NCERT for staying free of sexually transmitted infections?
options: Avoiding sex with unknown or multiple partners
Always trying to use condoms during coitus
Consulting a qualified doctor in case of doubt and completing the treatment
Taking oral contraceptive pills regularly
questions.explanation:
NCERT gives three principles for preventing STIs.
(i) Avoid sex with unknown or multiple partners.
(ii) Always try to use condoms during coitus.
(iii) In case of doubt, see a qualified doctor for early detection and complete treatment.
Oral pills only prevent conception, by inhibiting ovulation and implantation. They form no physical barrier against pathogens, so they give no protection from STIs.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Although everyone is vulnerable to sexually transmitted infections, their incidence is reported to be very high in which age group?
options: 5–14 years
15–24 years
25–34 years
35–49 years
questions.explanation:
NCERT notes that STI incidence is reported to be very high among persons aged 15–24 years. This is the adolescent and young adult group.
For this reason, awareness about safe practices and early detection is especially important for this group.
The other age ranges are not identified in the text as the high-incidence group.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Under the MTP (Amendment) Act, 2017, a pregnancy of 16 weeks may be terminated on permitted grounds on the opinion of a single registered medical practitioner.
Statement II: MTPs performed in the second trimester are much riskier than those performed in the first trimester.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. One registered medical practitioner's opinion is enough only up to 12 weeks. A 16-week pregnancy falls in the 12–24 week range, which needs the good-faith opinion of two registered medical practitioners.
Statement II is correct. NCERT says MTPs are relatively safe up to 12 weeks (first trimester), while second-trimester abortions are much riskier.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A mother who fully breast-feeds her infant soon after parturition has almost no chance of conceiving, so this can serve as a natural contraceptive method.
Reason (R): Ovulation, and therefore the menstrual cycle, does not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. This is the lactational amenorrhea method, which NCERT reports to be effective for up to a maximum of six months after parturition.
R is true. During intense lactation, ovulation does not take place, so the menstrual cycle also does not occur.
R explains A. Without ovulation there is no ovum to be fertilised, so conception is almost nil.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to NCERT, a woman using oral contraceptive pills should take them daily for how many days before taking a break?
options: 7 days
14 days
21 days
28 days
questions.explanation:
Pills are taken daily for 21 days.
This is followed by a 7-day gap during which menstruation occurs, and then the same pattern is repeated.
28 days is a tempting choice, but it is the 21 days of pills plus the 7-day gap, not the number of days the pills are taken.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about medical termination of pregnancy (MTP) is incorrect?
options: Government of India legalised MTP in 1971 with strict conditions to avoid its misuse
Under the MTP (Amendment) Act, 2017, a pregnancy of 12 to 24 weeks can be terminated on certain grounds only if two registered medical practitioners agree
Nearly 45 to 50 million MTPs are performed worldwide every year, about one-fifth of all conceived pregnancies
Second trimester abortions are considered safer than abortions performed in the first trimester
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: MTP was legalised in India in 1971.
(2) Correct: for pregnancies of more than 12 but fewer than 24 weeks, two registered medical practitioners must form the opinion that the grounds exist.
(3) Correct: NCERT gives 45 to 50 million MTPs a year, about 1/5th of conceived pregnancies.
(4) Incorrect: MTPs are relatively safe in the first trimester (up to 12 weeks). Second trimester abortions are much riskier.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to NCERT, the use of condoms has increased in recent years mainly because, besides preventing conception, they:
options: make the uterus unsuitable for implantation
can be reused many times
protect the user from contracting STIs and AIDS
inhibit ovulation in the female partner
questions.explanation:
NCERT says condom use has risen because of an additional benefit: protection from STIs and AIDS.
Condoms are disposable, not reusable. Reusability is a feature of diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults.
Making the uterus unsuitable for implantation is an action of hormone-releasing IUDs.
Inhibiting ovulation is an action of oral pills.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Lippes loop
(B) Multiload 375
(C) LNG-20
(D) Saheli
List-II
(i) Hormone-releasing IUD
(ii) Once-a-week non-steroidal oral pill
(iii) Non-medicated IUD
(iv) Copper-releasing IUD
Choose the correct option.
options: A-(iii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(ii)
A-(iv), B-(iii), C-(i), D-(ii)
A-(iii), B-(i), C-(iv), D-(ii)
A-(i), B-(iv), C-(iii), D-(ii)
questions.explanation:
(A) Lippes loop is non-medicated, so it matches (iii).
(B) Multiload 375 releases copper, like CuT and Cu7, so it matches (iv).
(C) LNG-20 releases a hormone, like Progestasert, so it matches (i).
(D) Saheli is a once-a-week, non-steroidal oral pill developed at CDRI Lucknow, so it matches (ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Amniocentesis continues to have a legitimate medical use even though its use for sex determination is legally banned in India.
Reason (R): Analysis of fetal cells and dissolved substances in amniotic fluid can reveal genetic disorders such as Down syndrome and sickle-cell anaemia.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. The ban targets only the use of amniocentesis for sex determination, to check female foeticide. The procedure itself is not outlawed.
R is true. NCERT states that amniocentesis tests for genetic disorders such as Down syndrome, haemophilia and sickle-cell anaemia.
R explains A, because this diagnostic value is exactly why the procedure remains medically useful.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 · Reproductive Health
